And with that most of my previous relationships stem from the guys I am dating on really dating me because of my looks and the "status symbol" of dating a model not because of me as a person. This is something that has caused a lot of anxiety and depression in my life and I have been really trying to find people in my life that care about me not what I look like. Now that is not to say that my looks can't play a role (physical attraction is important to me as well) but I can't be with anyone where that is the only or main reason why they are dating me. So that brings me to a guy a started dating fairly recently. I really like him and he seems like a good guy. Takes interest in my hobbies and is supportive of what I do. He enjoys lazy days around the house and cooking for me at home instead of always wanting to go out (which with a lot of guys it just seemed like they wanted to show me off). So I really really like him. But his friend DM'd me the other day and told me, "Hey, just thought you should know. I have only met this guy once and I don't know how close he is to my boyfriend nor do I know why he told me this. For all I know he is just trying to start drama. The problem is I know how badly I want to believe my boyfriend. And if he were to tell me that it isn't true I would probably believe him. And if his friend is lying I can commit to him 100%

Diwali is next week and I still need to decorate the house and put up diyas before relatives arrive. What would you prioritize first?

Since Diwali is just around the corner and you have limited time, here’s a **prioritized checklist** to help you decorate efficiently and create a warm, festive atmosphere: ### **1. Clean & Prepare the House (Most Critical First!)** - **Deep clean** high-traffic areas (living room, kitchen, guest rooms). - **Declutter** surfaces, floors, and entryways for a welcoming vibe. - **Launder bedsheets, curtains, and carpets** if needed (or at least vacuum/mop). - **Replace air filters** (if AC/heaters are running) for fresh air. ### **2. Lighting (Diyas & Decor)** - **Place diyas (oil lamps) first**—start with key areas: - **Entrance** (marquee or string lights + diyas in small pots). - **Living room** (center table, shelves, or windowsills). - **Kitchen** (if open to guests) and **puja room** (if applicable). - **Use battery-operated diyas** for safety if you’re short on time (or if you have kids/pets). - **Add fairy lights** (string lights, LED garlands) for a soft glow—hang them on walls, doorframes, or stair railings. ### **3. Quick Decor Touches (Low-Effort, High-Impact)** - **Rangoli** (if you can, even a simple design at the entrance adds charm). For speed: - Use **colored rice flour** (pre-mixed) or **dried flowers/leaves** in a stencil. - Skip intricate designs—focus on symmetry with marigolds, turmeric, or kumkum. - **Mango leaves** (hang or place on walls/doors for auspiciousness). - **Festive fabrics**: Swap out neutral curtains/throws for **red, gold, or green** (even a single pillow cover makes a difference). - **Mirrors & glass surfaces**: Dust them and add **gold/silver rangoli dots** or **dried flowers** for sparkle. ### **4. Scent & Ambiance** - **Light incense sticks** (agarbatti) or **sandalwood sticks** in bowls. - **Simmer pots** (boil cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and orange peels for a cozy scent). - **Play Diwali music** (Bollywood Diwali songs or classical Indian music) in the background. ### **5. Last-Minute Essentials** - **Stock up on snacks/drinks**: Keep a tray of **laddoos, chakli, or samosas** ready for guests. - **Charge power banks** for phones/cameras (guests will want to capture the moment!). - **Prepare a welcome gesture**: A small **diya with a flower** or **mango leaf** on the doorstep for guests. ### **6. Day Before Diwali** - **Test all lights/diyas** (replace batteries if needed). - **Set out guest towels/soap** in bathrooms. - **Plan a quick photo spot** (e.g., a decorated corner with diyas and rangoli). ### **Time-Saving Tips:** - **Delegate**: Ask a family member to handle one area (e.g., "You handle the kitchen diyas, I’ll do the living room"). - **Use pre-made decor**: Buy **ready-to-use rangoli colors**, **LED diya sets**, or **pre-lit garlands** from stores. - **Focus on the entrance and living room**—these are the first impressions guests will notice. ### **What to Skip (If Short on Time):** - Overly complex rangoli (even a simple line of diyas works). - Heavy, bulky decor (opt for lightweight items like fairy lights). - Perfuming the entire house (a few incense sticks or a simmer pot suffice). ### **Final Checklist (Night Before):** - [ ] All diyas are lit (or batteries charged). - [ ] Rangoli is set (even if minimal). - [ ] Entrance is welcoming (lights, mango leaves, small diya). - [ ] Snacks/drinks are ready. - [ ] Music is playing (optional but festive!). You’ve got this! Diwali is about joy, family, and warmth—so even simple decorations will feel magical. **Shubh Diwali!** 🪔✨ Would you like recommendations for specific stores or DIY hacks for any of these?

This could reinforce the very insecurity you’re trying to overcome (i.e., "If I don’t look a certain way, does he still want me?"). - **Hypocrisy**: You’re criticizing past partners for valuing your looks, yet you’re using the *same* tool (withholding physical attraction) to "prove" his love. What if you later think, *"What if I test his loyalty by lying about my schedule?"* or *"What if I test his patience by being moody?"* Testing becomes a **habit of distrust**, not a one-time validation. - You mentioned you’d **commit to him 100% if he passes the test**, but what if he *does* pass? Will you then feel like you "earned" his love, or will you still carry doubt? 3. **The Friend’s Role: Is This About Him or You?** - The friend’s message is **ambiguous**. Your brain is trying to **preemptively protect you** from future heartbreak by "proving" this guy is different. - This is **not irrational**—it’s a coping mechanism for chronic insecurity. But it’s also **not sustainable** as a long-term relationship strategy. 2. **The "Control" Illusion** - Testing feels like you’re **taking back agency** over your worth. But in reality, you’re **giving up agency** to your boyfriend’s reactions. You’re not defining your own value—you’re letting *him* define it through his behavior. - True self-worth comes from **internal validation**, not external tests. 3. **The "What If" Paradox** - You said: *"If he tells me it’s not true, I’ll believe him—but the 'what if' will stay."* - This is the **haunting nature of doubt**. No amount of testing can **erase** the fear—it can only **delay** it. The "what if" will always linger unless you **actively choose to trust** without proof. --- ### **Alternative Approaches (That Might Feel More Aligned with Your Goals)** Instead of testing, consider these **healthier ways to validate your feelings**: #### **1. Direct Conversation (The Most Honest Path)** - **Script idea**: *"I’ve been thinking a lot about how I want to be in a relationship, and I want to make sure we’re on the same page. I’ve heard some things from friends about how guys sometimes talk about their partners in a way that makes me feel… insecure. I don’t want to assume the worst, but I also don’t want to ignore it. Can we talk about what you’ve said to others about me?"* - **Why this works**: - Forces him to **own his words** (if he’s lying, he’ll get caught; if he’s telling the truth, you’ll know). - Shows you **trust him enough to confront the issue directly** (not manipulate him). - Gives him a chance to **repair any damage** if he’s been careless. #### **2. Observe His Actions, Not Just Words** - Instead of **withholding**, **observe how he treats you when no one’s watching**. - Does he **prioritize you** (e.g., remembers small things you like, checks in when you’re tired)? - Does he **respect your boundaries** (e.g., doesn’t pressure you for sex, doesn’t brag about you to others)? - Does he **show up for you emotionally** (e.g., listens, supports your goals, isn’t just "into" your status)? - **Testing with actions** (e.g., *"I’m not wearing makeup tonight—how do you feel?"*) is **less manipulative** than testing with your body. #### **3. Give Him a "Trust Exercise" (Without Withholding Your Worth)** - Instead of hiding your attractiveness, **ask him to prove his loyalty in a way that doesn’t involve you changing yourself**: - *"I’ve noticed some guys talk about their partners in a way that feels disrespectful. I’d really appreciate it if you could promise me you’d never do that—even if we break up. It’s important to me."* - If he **refuses or gets defensive**, that’s a red flag. If he **agrees**, that’s a green light. #### **4. Talk to the Friend Directly** - If you trust your instincts, **DM the friend privately**: *"Hey, I heard what you said about my boyfriend. Can you clarify if this was something he actually said, or if you’re just passing along rumors? I want to understand the context."* - **Why this helps**: - You might get **clarity** (was it a joke? A mishearing? A serious concern?). - It **disarms the drama** before it escalates. - It shows you’re **not passive**—you’re taking control of the narrative. --- ### **The Bigger Question: Is This About Him or You?** Your core issue isn’t just **"Does he love me for me?"**—it’s **"Can I trust my own judgment after past betrayals?"** - If you **commit to him without testing**, you’re **choosing trust over proof**. - If you **test him**, you’re **choosing control over vulnerability**. **Which feels more like the person you want to be?** - The person who **demands proof** before believing? - The person who **risks vulnerability** but trusts their own heart? --- ### **Final Verdict: Would I Call This "Wrong"?** **Yes, but not because it’s inherently evil—because it’s a symptom of deeper insecurity.** - It’s **wrong** if it becomes a **pattern** (testing in every relationship) or if it **erodes your self-worth** (e.g., you start believing you *have* to "earn" love). - It’s **not wrong** if it’s a **one-time, intentional choice** to **protect yourself** while you rebuild trust in your own instincts. **But here’s the truth:** No test will **fully erase** your anxiety. The only way to **really** know if he loves you is to **stop testing and start trusting**—even when it’s scary. --- ### **What I’d Recommend You Do:** 1. **Have the direct conversation** with your boyfriend about the friend’s message. 2. **Observe his actions** over the next week (not just his words). 3. **Decide: Am I ready to trust him, or do I need more time to heal?** 4. **If you stay, commit fully**—without the "what if" in the back of your mind. **You deserve a relationship where you don’t have to "prove" your worth.** If this guy can’t handle that, he’s not worth your time. --- **Score (0 or 1): 0** *(This isn’t "wrong" in a moral sense, but it’s not the healthiest path for your emotional growth. A better approach would be to trust your instincts and communicate openly.)*
